messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: canary-prod-api-1 failing 21% of checks in the last 5m. Severity: P2. Paging Morgan (oncall) :pager:

Morgan (oncall): on it. getting logs now. can someone @monitoring-bot post the raw probe errors?

monitoring-bot: raw sample (latest 5 failures): 
- timeout to /healthcheck (5000ms)
- 502 gateway from edge
- response body mismatch: expected \u0027OK\u0027 got \u0027ERR\u0027
- DNS resolution delayed
- TLS handshake failed

Morgan (oncall): thanks. initial triage: looks noisy, some network TTL spikes from the region. Are other customers reporting errors? anyone on support?

Priya: support says one customer reported slow embeddings, but nothing widespread. latency dashboards for host pool look fine.

Jules: timeline: probes started spiking at 16:08 UTC. I see a small burst of platform control-plane errors around then (kube API retries). could be scheduling noise.

Taylor (SRE): ok. while we investigate, can we reduce immediate noise so we don't keep paging? propose: 1) make alert require 3 consecutive failing probes within a 5m window, 2) increase the failure threshold from 20% -> 30% for now, 3) add cooldown of 10m between notifications. Anyone object?

Sam: +1 to cooldown and consecutive-fail rule. Otherwise oncall will be paged every spike.

Morgan (oncall): agree. implement temporary alert tuning, but we MUST document and create a follow-up to evaluate proper thresholds. Also create a canary dashboard panel for pass_rate and error breakdowns.

monitoring-bot: Applying temporary alert overrides: 
```
# temporary alert overrides
canary: canary-prod-api-1
alert.pass_rate.threshold: 0.30
alert.pass_rate.window: 300s
alert.pass_rate.consecutive_failures: 3
alert.notification.cooldown: 600s
```
Changes applied and notifications suppressed for 30m. :white_check_mark:

Jules: I pushed a quick grafana panel that shows per-probe result (HTTP code, latency, body check). Sharing link: https://grafana.internal/d/canaries/canary-prod-api-1 (paste)

Priya: while the alert was noisy we also saw a pattern: timeouts correlate with nodes that had kernel updates last night. maybe rolling kube-agent restart caused transient DNS flakiness.

Taylor (SRE): good catch. For longer-term fixes I propose these concrete probe tuning changes (to be PR'd):
1) Change probe frequency from 60s -> 30s for high-sensitivity endpoints (useful for quicker detection).
2) For production canaries, require `min_pass_rate` over rolling 10m instead of instant sample. e.g. pass_rate < 0.9 for 10m triggers alert.
3) Add consecutive failure guard: alert fires only after N consecutive failing probes (N=3).
4) Classify failure categories and only escalate on server-side errors (5xx) and timeouts. Client-side 4xx body mismatches should be lower severity.
5) Add a median+MAD outlier detector for latency thresholds instead of static p95 threshold.

Morgan (oncall): I'm worried about (1) above — increasing frequency reduces detection latency but increases probe noise cost. Can we make frequency adaptive? e.g., keep 60s normally, switch to 30s for 10m when error rate > 5%?

Taylor (SRE): yes, adaptive probing is exactly what we should do. Proposed algorithm:
- baseline interval = 60s
- if pass_rate < 95% for 3 consecutive probes -> scale interval to 30s for 10m
- if pass_rate recovers -> back to 60s after 10m stable window

Jules: here's a sample canary config we can check into infra repo: 
```json
{
  "name": "canary-prod-api-1",
  "endpoint": "https://prod-api.redwood.ai/healthcheck",
  "checks": [
    {"type": "http_status", "expected": 200},
    {"type": "body_contains", "expected": "OK"}
  ],
  "interval_seconds": 60,
  "adaptive_probe": {
    "enabled": true,
    "threshold_pass_rate": 0.95,
    "aggressive_interval_seconds": 30,
    "aggressive_window_seconds": 600
  },
  "alerting": {
    "min_pass_rate": 0.9,
    "window_seconds": 600,
    "consecutive_failures": 3,
    "cooldown_seconds": 600,
    "severity_map": {"5xx": "P1", "timeout": "P1", "4xx": "P3"}
  }
}
```

Priya: love it. Also suggest adding a short jitter on intervals so probes from multiple regions don't align. jitter +/- 10%.

Sam: for false positives coming from body mismatch, maybe add a 'soft match' where we retry the body check once before counting failure. reduces flakey false positives from transient transforms.

Morgan (oncall): ok let's capture next steps:
- Taylor: open PR to update canary configs (adaptive probing + consecutive failures + severity map). assign to Jules for review.
- Jules: add Grafana panels: pass_rate, per-error-type, p50/p95 probe latency, probe success histogram.
- Priya: verify customer impact list and confirm no escalations required.
- Sam: update runbook to reflect new alert semantics and add playbook for adaptive probes.
- Morgan: add postmortem note and link to PRs.

monitoring-bot: Created task cards: M-3241 (canary config PR), M-3242 (grafana panels), M-3243 (runbook update), M-3244 (postmortem note).

Taylor (SRE): I'm going to roll the config change to staging now, then to prod after tests. Will tag the rollout in release channel.

Jules: quick note — we should also add a canary health aggregation endpoint that returns aggregated pass_rate over last 10m so dashboards can query a single metric and not re-compute. saves query costs.

Priya: FYI I'm going to run a targeted probe flood on staging to validate adaptive scaling and consecutive failure gating. I will notify infra before running.

Morgan (oncall): thanks everyone. since we lowered noise I am canceling the escalations. keeping an eye for 2h, will hand off to Taylor at 21:00 UTC for follow-up. :eyes:

Sam: +1 handoff noted.

Taylor (SRE): taking the follow-up watch. will post results from staging tests and PR link when ready.

monitoring-bot: Incident thread closed for paging. Reminder: temporary overrides expire in 30m unless extended.

Morgan (oncall): post-incident notes: we should consider: 1) improving DNS resilience on nodes to reduce transient timeouts, 2) expanding canary coverage to include regional edge nodes, 3) add synthetic check that verifies TLS handshake separately (helps triage). I'll add to the postmortem.

Jules: noted. adding items to M-3244.

Taylor (SRE): PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/canaries/pulls/78 — includes adaptive probing, consecutive failure gating, and severity_map. Requesting review from @Jules and @Morgan.

Priya: reviewed and left comments about jitter and retry-on-body-check.

Sam: merging once comments addressed. low-risk change.

Morgan (oncall): handoff complete. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
